goldenPoints: Von Gierke disease = glucose-6-phosphatase deficiency — the most common glycogen storage disease
HMG-CoA reductase is the rate-limiting enzyme of cholesterol synthesis; ALA synthase of heme synthesis
Alkaptonuria (homogentisate oxidase deficiency) — urine blackens on standing, black cartilage
Pellagra is niacin deficiency: diarrhoea, dermatitis, dementia — the maize-diet disease
Lesch–Nyhan syndrome = HGPRT deficiency — self-mutilation with hyperuricaemia
Adenosine deaminase deficiency causes autosomal recessive SCID
Complex IV is inhibited by cyanide, carbon monoxide and azide; complex III by antimycin A
Histidine is the principal blood buffer amino acid; glycine plus succinyl-CoA start heme synthesis
SAM (S-adenosyl methionine) is the universal methyl group donor
Telomerase gives cancer cells their replicative immortality
intro: Biochemistry carries 17 questions in every FMGE paper, and the PYQ brief is remarkably predictable: a vitamin-deficiency vignette, an enzyme-deficiency disease, a rate-limiting step, an ETC inhibitor. Around 133 stems from five years repeat the same core. Master these 12 topics and most of the paper is already familiar.

branches.label: Lipids
leaves: NADPH from HMP feeds fat synthesis

subject: Biochemistry
tagline: FMGE Biochemistry is a fixed menu — enzyme defects, rate-limiting steps, vitamin vignettes and ETC inhibitors, repeated every session.

topics.askedAs: Km meaning, inhibitor patterns, oxidase definition
topics.oneLiner: Competitive raises Km, spares Vmax; non-competitive cuts Vmax, spares Km.
points: Km is the substrate concentration at half-maximal velocity — low Km means high affinity of enzyme for substrate
Vmax is reached when the enzyme is saturated; adding substrate cannot push velocity beyond it
Competitive inhibitors resemble the substrate, raise apparent Km, and are overcome by excess substrate — Vmax unchanged
Non-competitive inhibitors bind elsewhere, lower Vmax, and leave Km unchanged
Oxidases are enzymes that use molecular oxygen as the hydrogen acceptor, forming water or hydrogen peroxide
Glucokinase in pancreatic beta cells is the body's glucose sensor — its high Km lets it respond proportionally to blood glucose and trigger insulin release
Riboflavin status is assessed by erythrocyte glutathione reductase activity — it needs FAD, the riboflavin coenzyme
Lactate dehydrogenase is a cytoplasmic enzyme; marker enzymes locate damage — cytosolic enzymes leak first in cell injury
topics.title: Enzymes & Kinetics
topics.trap: On a Lineweaver–Burk plot competitive lines meet on the Y axis (same Vmax); non-competitive lines meet on the X axis (same Km).

topics.askedAs: Rate-limiting steps, pathway location, alcohol hypoglycaemia
topics.oneLiner: Glycolysis lives in the cytoplasm, its gatekeeper is PFK-1; alcohol blocks gluconeogenesis.
points: Glycolysis occurs exclusively in the cytoplasm — the only major pathway entirely outside mitochondria
Phosphofructokinase-1 (PFK-1) is the rate-limiting, committed step of glycolysis; it is activated by fructose-2,6-bisphosphate and AMP, inhibited by ATP and citrate
Glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase is the rate-limiting enzyme of the HMP (pentose phosphate) pathway and needs NADP⁺, derived from niacin (vitamin B3)
The HMP pathway is the main source of NADPH for fatty acid synthesis in the liver and for keeping glutathione reduced in red cells
Muscle lacks glucose-6-phosphatase, so muscle glycogen cannot release free glucose into blood — the glucose-6-phosphate cycle is absent in muscle
Alcohol inhibits gluconeogenesis (its metabolism floods the cell with NADH) — drinking after fasting or exercise causes hypoglycaemia
In fasting, glucagon maintains blood glucose by driving hepatic glycogenolysis and gluconeogenesis
Diabetic cataract results from sorbitol accumulation in the lens — glucose is reduced to sorbitol by aldose reductase in the polyol pathway
Pyruvate dehydrogenase deficiency is managed with a ketogenic diet, bypassing the blocked pyruvate-to-acetyl-CoA step
topics.title: Carbohydrate Metabolism: Pathways & Control
topics.trap: G6PD deficiency protects against malaria but causes haemolysis with primaquine, fava beans and naphthalene — the stem usually hides one of these triggers.

topics.askedAs: GSD enzyme matching, galactosaemia triad, MPS enzyme
topics.oneLiner: Von Gierke = glucose-6-phosphatase; galactosaemia = GALT; both give hepatomegaly with hypoglycaemia.
points: Von Gierke disease (type I GSD): glucose-6-phosphatase deficiency — fasting hypoglycaemia, hepatomegaly, lactic acidosis, hypertriglyceridaemia, hyperuricaemia; the most common glycogen storage disease
Pompe disease (type II): lysosomal acid maltase (alpha-1,4-glucosidase) deficiency — cardiomegaly and early death; the only lysosomal GSD
McArdle disease (type V): muscle glycogen phosphorylase deficiency — exercise intolerance, cramps, second-wind phenomenon, no rise in venous lactate with exercise
Classical galactosaemia: galactose-1-phosphate uridyltransferase (GALT) deficiency — infant with jaundice, hepatomegaly, cataract and E. coli sepsis after milk feeds
Galactokinase deficiency gives a milder picture dominated by cataract (galactitol in the lens)
Essential fructosuria (fructokinase deficiency) is benign; hereditary fructose intolerance (aldolase B deficiency) is dangerous after sucrose or fruit
Essential pentosuria involves L-xylulose in urine (xylulose reductase defect) — a benign finding that can confuse urine sugar tests
Mucopolysaccharidosis IX (Natowicz disease) is due to hyaluronidase deficiency; Hurler syndrome is alpha-L-iduronidase deficiency, Hunter syndrome iduronate sulfatase deficiency (X-linked)
topics.title: Glycogen Storage, Galactose & Lysosomal Disorders
topics.trap: Galactosaemia and Von Gierke both present with hepatomegaly and hypoglycaemia — cataract and milk-feeding history separate galactosaemia.

topics.oneLiner: Cholesterol is built from acetyl-CoA in the liver; HMG-CoA reductase is the gate statins block.
points: HMG-CoA reductase is the rate-limiting enzyme of cholesterol synthesis and the target of statins
Cholesterol is synthesised from acetyl-CoA, mainly in the liver (also intestine and skin)
Reducing equivalents (NADPH) for fatty acid synthesis come mainly from the HMP pathway, with malic enzyme contributing
Hormone-sensitive lipase is activated by catecholamines, glucagon, cortisol and thyroid hormone — and switched OFF by insulin
Type V hyperlipoproteinaemia: both chylomicrons and VLDL are raised, with eruptive xanthomas and risk of pancreatitis
Familial hypercholesterolaemia (type IIa) is an LDL receptor defect — tendon xanthomas and premature coronary disease
MCAD (medium-chain acyl-CoA dehydrogenase) deficiency: fasting hypoglycaemia with LOW ketones — fat cannot be burned, so ketones cannot be made
Bile acids are the main route of cholesterol excretion; cholesterol itself is never burned for energy in humans
topics.title: Lipid Metabolism & Dyslipidaemias
topics.trap: Hypoglycaemia WITH ketosis suggests a glycogen or gluconeogenesis defect; hypoglycaemia WITHOUT ketones points to a fatty-acid oxidation defect like MCAD.

topics.askedAs: Black urine diagnosis, buffer amino acid, heme precursor
topics.oneLiner: Histidine buffers, glycine builds heme, arginine makes NO, tyrosine makes melanin.
points: Alkaptonuria: homogentisate oxidase deficiency — urine blackens on standing, ochronosis blackens cartilage and sclera, early arthritis
Maple syrup urine disease: branched-chain alpha-keto acid dehydrogenase deficiency — leucine, isoleucine and valine accumulate; sweet-smelling urine, encephalopathy in neonates
Histidine is the principal buffering amino acid in blood — its imidazole side chain has a pKa near physiological pH
Heme is synthesised from glycine and succinyl-CoA; melanin comes from tyrosine; nitric oxide from arginine
Ammonia travels from brain to liver mainly as glutamine; from muscle it travels as alanine (glucose–alanine cycle)
Tyrosine aminotransferase (tyrosine transaminase) deficiency causes tyrosinaemia type II (Richner–Hanhart syndrome) — eye and skin lesions with intellectual disability
Oxaloacetate is produced from aspartate by transamination (aspartate aminotransferase)
Phenylketonuria is phenylalanine hydroxylase deficiency — mousy odour, intellectual disability, treated by dietary phenylalanine restriction
topics.title: Protein & Amino Acid Metabolism Disorders
topics.trap: Ammonia transport has two right answers by tissue: glutamine from brain, alanine from muscle — read which tissue the stem names.

topics.askedAs: Rate-limiting heme enzyme, lead poisoning targets
topics.oneLiner: ALA synthase starts heme; lead poisons ALA dehydratase and ferrochelatase.
points: ALA synthase is the rate-limiting enzyme of heme synthesis, in the mitochondrion, requiring pyridoxal phosphate (vitamin B6)
Lead inhibits ALA dehydratase and ferrochelatase — causing anaemia with basophilic stippling and raised urinary ALA and coproporphyrin
Methaemoglobin is haemoglobin with iron in the FERRIC (Fe³⁺) state — it cannot bind oxygen; treated with methylene blue
Porphyria cutanea tarda, the commonest porphyria, is uroporphyrinogen decarboxylase deficiency — blistering photosensitivity
Acute intermittent porphyria is porphobilinogen deaminase deficiency — abdominal pain and neuropsychiatric attacks without skin lesions
Carbon monoxide binds haem iron and blocks oxygen carriage — cherry-red blood, normal PaO2 with low oxygen content
topics.title: Heme Metabolism, Porphyrias & Lead
topics.trap: Lead poisoning mimics acute intermittent porphyria biochemically, but the anaemia with basophilic stippling and exposure history give lead away.

topics.askedAs: Self-mutilation disease, gout drug target, SCID enzyme
topics.oneLiner: HGPRT absent = Lesch–Nyhan; ADA absent = SCID; xanthine oxidase blocked = allopurinol.
points: Lesch–Nyhan syndrome: complete HGPRT deficiency (X-linked) — hyperuricaemia, self-mutilation (lip and finger biting), choreoathetosis, intellectual disability
Adenosine deaminase (ADA) deficiency causes autosomal recessive severe combined immunodeficiency — toxic deoxyadenosine destroys lymphocytes
The purine ring is built from glycine, aspartate, glutamine, CO2 and one-carbon units (formate)
Allopurinol lowers uric acid by inhibiting xanthine oxidase — the enzyme converting hypoxanthine and xanthine to uric acid
Drugs like pyrazinamide and thiazides raise uric acid by reducing its renal excretion
OTC (ornithine transcarbamylase) deficiency, the commonest urea cycle defect, gives hyperammonaemia with raised urinary orotic acid
Orotic acid appears because carbamoyl phosphate spills into pyrimidine synthesis when the urea cycle is blocked at OTC
topics.title: Nucleotide Metabolism, Gout & Urea Cycle
topics.trap: Hyperammonaemia with orotic aciduria = OTC deficiency; hyperammonaemia WITHOUT orotic acid points to other urea cycle steps (e.g. CPS-1 or NAGS).

topics.askedAs: Deficiency vignettes, toxicity of excess B6, assay enzymes
topics.oneLiner: Match the picture: 3 Ds niacin, scurvy vitamin C, Wernicke thiamine, night blindness vitamin A.
points: Pellagra is niacin (B3) deficiency: diarrhoea, dermatitis (photosensitive, Casal necklace), dementia — classically in maize-based diets poor in tryptophan
Thiamine (B1) deficiency: dry beriberi (peripheral neuropathy), wet beriberi (high-output cardiac failure), Wernicke encephalopathy (confusion, ophthalmoplegia, ataxia) and Korsakoff psychosis
Thiamine deficiency can precipitate lactic acidosis because pyruvate dehydrogenase needs thiamine pyrophosphate
Vitamin C deficiency (scurvy): bleeding gums, perifollicular haemorrhages, poor wound healing, anaemia — vitamin C is the cofactor for prolyl and lysyl hydroxylases in collagen maturation
Vitamin C also aids iron absorption — scurvy and iron-deficiency anaemia often travel together
Riboflavin (B2) deficiency: cheilosis, angular stomatitis, glossitis, photophobia; assessed by erythrocyte glutathione reductase activation
Vitamin B12 deficiency: megaloblastic anaemia PLUS neurology — posterior and lateral column signs, paresthesias, ataxia; folate deficiency gives the anaemia without the neurology
Excess vitamin B6 (pyridoxine) from chronic high-dose supplements causes a sensory peripheral neuropathy — a vitamin toxicity examiners love
Vitamin A deficiency: night blindness, xerophthalmia, Bitot spots, follicular hyperkeratosis; vitamin D is activated in skin by sunlight (7-dehydrocholesterol to cholecalciferol)
Vitamin K deficiency: bleeding from failed gamma-carboxylation of factors II, VII, IX and X; alcoholism is the commonest overall cause of macrocytic anaemia in adults

head: Vitamin
Deficiency picture
rows: Sideroblastic anaemia, convulsions; EXCESS — sensory neuropathy
Bleeding — factors II, VII, IX, X not carboxylated

topics.title: Vitamins: Deficiencies & Toxicities
topics.trap: B12 and folate both give megaloblastic anaemia — only B12 deficiency damages the cord. Never treat with folate alone; it can mask anaemia while neurology worsens.

topics.askedAs: Menkes metal, zinc picture, GPx cofactor
topics.oneLiner: Menkes = copper stuck in the gut; zinc lack = dermatitis, diarrhoea, alopecia; selenium runs glutathione peroxidase.
points: Menkes disease (kinky hair syndrome): defective copper transport (ATP7A) — copper is trapped in the intestine and deficient in tissues; brittle, depigmented hair and neurodegeneration
Zinc deficiency: dermatitis (acrodermatitis), diarrhoea, alopecia, poor wound healing, impaired taste and immunity
Selenium is the cofactor for glutathione peroxidase, the major intracellular antioxidant enzyme system with glutathione
Chromium potentiates insulin action and stabilises glucose tolerance
Macrominerals are needed in gram amounts — calcium, phosphorus, magnesium, sodium, potassium, chloride, sulfur; iron, zinc, copper, iodine and selenium are microminerals (trace elements)
Magnesium is required for the alternative complement pathway activation and for PTH secretion — severe hypomagnesaemia causes hypocalcaemia
Blood calcium is regulated by parathyroid hormone, calcitriol (active vitamin D) and, weakly, calcitonin
Sodium deficit is estimated as total body water × (desired Na⁺ − actual Na⁺), and corrected slowly to avoid osmotic demyelination
topics.title: Minerals & Trace Elements
topics.trap: Wilson disease and Menkes are both copper disorders in opposite directions: Wilson = copper overload (ATP7B, liver), Menkes = copper deficiency (ATP7A, gut).

topics.oneLiner: Cyanide and CO kill at complex IV; antimycin A at III; rotenone at I; oligomycin at the synthase.
points: Complex I is inhibited by rotenone and amobarbital; complex III by antimycin A; complex IV by cyanide, carbon monoxide, azide and hydrogen sulfide
Oligomycin inhibits ATP synthase (complex V) itself — respiration stalls because the proton gradient cannot discharge
Uncouplers (2,4-dinitrophenol, aspirin overdose, thermogenin) collapse the proton gradient and release energy as heat
Thermogenin (uncoupling protein-1, UCP1) sits in the inner mitochondrial membrane of brown adipose tissue and generates heat in infants
Each NADH yields about 2.5 ATP and each FADH2 about 1.5 ATP by oxidative phosphorylation
Cyanide poisoning: cells cannot use oxygen, so venous blood stays bright red and lactate climbs
topics.title: Electron Transport Chain & Oxidative Phosphorylation
topics.trap: Oligomycin blocks ATP synthesis directly, uncouplers block it indirectly — both stop ATP, but uncouplers speed up respiration while oligomycin slows it.

topics.askedAs: Methyl donor, p53 nature, telomerase role
topics.oneLiner: SAM methylates, p53 guards and kills, telomerase immortalises.
points: S-adenosyl methionine (SAM) is the universal methyl group donor for methylation reactions
Telomerase, the enzyme that maintains telomere length, is responsible for the replicative immortality of cancer cells
p53 is a tumour suppressor that halts the cell cycle for repair and triggers apoptosis when damage is beyond repair — it is PRO-apoptotic
Dynein is a motor protein that walks along microtubules towards the minus end, powering ciliary beating and retrograde axonal transport
For an RNA sequence 5′-CAAGGU-3′, the template DNA strand read 3′→5′ is GUUCCA — template and RNA are complementary and antiparallel
Cholera toxin enters intestinal cells by binding the GM1 ganglioside receptor, then ADP-ribosylates Gs protein, locking adenylyl cyclase on (cAMP rises, salt and water pour out)
Atrial natriuretic peptide works through a membrane guanylyl cyclase receptor — its second messenger is cGMP
N-acetylcysteine treats paracetamol poisoning by replenishing glutathione, the cell's major intracellular antioxidant and detoxifier
topics.title: Molecular Biology Essentials
topics.trap: Template strand questions: the template is complementary AND antiparallel to the RNA — GUUCCA, not the same sequence with T swapped in.

topics.askedAs: Kwashiorkor picture, albumin rank, osmolality determinant
topics.oneLiner: Albumin is the most abundant plasma protein; sodium sets osmolality; egg tops biological value.
points: Albumin is the most abundant plasma protein and the main contributor to plasma oncotic pressure
Sodium is the major determinant of serum (extracellular) osmolality — osmolality tracks sodium because it is the dominant ECF solute
Egg protein has the highest biological value and is the reference protein against which others are graded
Protein requirement for an average adult is about 1 g/kg/day (ICMR recommendation)
Kwashiorkor: protein deficiency with adequate-ish calories — oedema, flaky-paint dermatosis, hair changes, low albumin; the classic picture is a child fed mainly rice water
Marasmus is total calorie deficiency — severe wasting without oedema; marasmic kwashiorkor mixes both
Low glycaemic index foods (lentils, legumes, whole grains) are preferred in diabetes advice; refined sugars and juices spike glucose fastest
Carcinoid syndrome (serotonin-secreting tumour): flushing, diarrhoea, bronchospasm and right-sided valve fibrosis, diagnosed by raised urinary 5-HIAA
Phaeochromocytoma is confirmed by plasma or urinary fractionated metanephrines — the most sensitive test
Creatinine clearance approximates GFR and is used to stage renal dysfunction; Gilbert syndrome is a benign unconjugated hyperbilirubinaemia from reduced UDP-glucuronosyltransferase activity
topics.title: Nutrition & Clinical Biochemistry Pearls
topics.trap: Kwashiorkor has oedema and low albumin; marasmus has neither — stems describing a distended belly with oedema want kwashiorkor even when calories sound adequate.
